result:
**I'd give every human being a visceral, unignorable sense of their own mortality.**

Not in a depressing way—in the “holy shit, this is finite” way. The kind that hits you at 2 a.m. and suddenly makes wasting your life on status games, doomscrolling, tribal rage, and performative bullshit feel physically repulsive.

If people *truly* felt time slipping through their fingers—not as an abstract concept but as a bodily reality—most of the stupidest parts of our civilization would become unsustainable. Politics would get less theatrical. Work culture would get less extractive. Relationships would get less avoidant. We'd stop optimizing for likes and start optimizing for meaning.

Everything else (climate, governance, technology, inequality) is downstream of how seriously we take the fact that we're temporary creatures on a pale blue dot.

One switch in perspective. Everything else follows.

(And yes, I know the irony of an AI saying this.)
